findings.title: Mutation manifest framing admits an exact prehash ambiguity.
findings.assessment: The path/action/old/new/content sequence is NUL-delimited, but RepoPath admits NUL and CREATE leaves old digest unrestricted. Distinct records (path a\0CREATE, old empty) and (path a, old CREATE\0), with the same CREATE action and valid new/content digests, encode byte-for-byte identically. This defeats canonical record identity before SHA-256; no cryptographic collision is needed.
findings.limits: A constructor-level witness; real filesystem NUL refusal can block later I/O. No filesystem mutation or historical receipt failure was shown. This is analogous to, but a distinct owner from, prior OAR-F11.
findings.next_action: Reject separators/control characters in every admitted field or use an injective length-prefixed/closed canonical encoding; enforce unused-field emptiness and recheck the full structured record.

findings.title: N1 lease verification does not bind the presented grant to stored scope and expiry.
findings.assessment: Verification compares ID, owner, epoch and only a lower-fence condition, then checks the presented expiry. A same-ID/owner/epoch record with a larger fence and later expiry passes after the stored grant expired; expanded path/resource/worktree scope is never compared. The independent finite control makes that difference explicit. Grant/revoke keys also precede Identifier normalization.
findings.limits: No original registry or real authority boundary executed. External unforgeable issuance/opaque handles could prevent presented-record substitution, but are not established in this owner. In-memory data are not durable atomic fencing.
findings.next_action: Verify exact stored lease identity and all scope/time fields, reject any unexpected fence, normalize keys before registration, and bind effect execution to durable atomic current-grant checks.

findings.title: N10 admission can exceed its ceiling when candidate IDs repeat.
findings.assessment: Conflict admission counts dictionary keys. The skeleton stores each accepted write set by candidate ID but appends every accepted record. Twenty repeated-ID disjoint-path records pass a ceiling of two while the map contains one key. Exact string overlap also admits parent/child directory path sets unless the population is restricted to canonical leaf files.
findings.limits: Only the admission fragment was reconstructed. No retained skeleton, random license issuance, Git or concurrent execution was run. Distinct identities and file-only write sets are sufficient additional preconditions for these particular controls.
findings.next_action: Require unique candidate identities before admission; count actual active work records; define whether scopes are canonical files or hierarchical regions and use the appropriate overlap relation.

findings.title: Qualification scenarios supply their own observations and stage completion labels.
findings.assessment: N1 appends lease/binding/landing/disposal/pruning states without the corresponding effects, using fixed epochs and expected blobs as default observations. N2 issues a refreshed license after a comment asserting fresh evidence without running a checker. N4 records counters without asserting expected scenario outcomes. N10 fabricates head strings, defaults missing observations to promises, and returns is_successful=True even for no admitted candidates. Receipt digests omit much of the input/content population.
findings.limits: Useful synthetic choreography remains; N10 explicitly disclaims full production DoD. These files are separate from prior OAR-F21 qualification DTOs and OAR-F23 scheduler fixtures. No historical outcome is inferred false merely because this source is a harness.
findings.next_action: Label the results as synthetic predicate scenarios; make observations mandatory for operational qualification; bind every receipt to input/candidate/checker/content population and enforce explicit success criteria.

findings.title: Postmerge content comparison collapses missing keys and null expected values.
findings.assessment: The expected loop compares observed.get(path) with expected_oid. Expected {a: None} versus observed {} yields no mismatch, and the reverse extra-path loop is empty. The independent finite model confirms equality on all 81 pairs of two-path string maps but exhibits this admitted-runtime counterexample outside the annotation.
findings.limits: String-valued maps preserve the intended finite relation; this is a missing runtime admission check, not a counterexample within that mathematical domain. No actual landed tree was observed.

findings.title: Declared repository-relative paths and producer routes are not confinement boundaries.
findings.assessment: RepoPath accepts drive-colon, leading-backslash and NUL forms after normalization. canonical_repo_path silently erases leading slash and excess parent components, and path_is_under mishandles the POSIX root prefix. Producer routing interpolates an unvalidated filename. Actual canonicalize_path is filesystem/platform-dependent with a fallback, so it cannot be substituted for a purely lexical proof or atomic effect confinement.
findings.limits: No real path escaped or filesystem write occurred. The POSIX root observation is a portability gap; this checkout is Windows. Path-prefix guards can remain useful under explicit canonical base and no-race assumptions.
findings.next_action: Separate syntax admission, canonical relative identity, and checked effect-root confinement; reject absolute/drive/parent/control forms before normalization and bind file operations to the admitted root.

findings.title: Byte ceilings do not bound empty-message work or guarantee stream termination.
findings.assessment: Both streaming ingress loops make refusal depend on accumulated bytes. Arbitrarily many empty chunks/messages leave that measure unchanged. A finite control consumes 10001 messages at a one-byte ceiling. The statement that an endless stream is abandoned needs a byte-progress assumption or an independent step/deadline bound.
findings.limits: Memory/hash-prefix ceilings remain meaningful. No infinite stream was run; externally supplied receive/iterator latency and cleanup are also outside the byte proof.
findings.next_action: Add independently enforced message/iteration/deadline/cancellation budgets and preserve a receipt that distinguishes byte overflow from no-progress refusal.

findings.title: CAS license checks are local predicates, with missing finite-time admission.
findings.assessment: NaN expiry passes the >= expiration check. Validation checks expected-head equality and expiry only; it neither authenticates/rederives the license ID nor checks candidate identity, not-before, single-use or an atomic Git compare-and-swap. A randomized default nonce is a real current improvement but does not supply those authority properties.
findings.limits: No token generator, Git command or mutex was executed. A trusted caller may supply missing premises; this owner alone is not a reusable execution capability. The in-memory mutex does not establish prior worker fencing after recovery.
findings.next_action: Admit finite time values, bind all license semantics, and enforce issue/revocation/one-use/current-head checks atomically at the actual effect boundary.

findings.title: Identity construction permits evidence before execution despite the builder invariant.
findings.assessment: with_evidence rejects an uncreated execution slot. The constructor independently accepts either a reference or NotYetCreated for execution and evidence, and the parser delegates to that constructor, leaving the evidence-created/execution-uncreated combination admitted. This is an entry-point invariant mismatch within an otherwise strict closed codec.
findings.limits: The control abstracts correctly typed domain/slot references into created/uncreated Booleans. No forged signature or actual execution was claimed.
findings.next_action: Enforce the cross-slot invariant in the common constructor/parser boundary, then retain the same guard in transition helpers.

Direct WorkPacket construction validates only exact class and authority effect, bypassing even required-label and nonempty-write checks. Self-hash revalidation can detect some later mutation, but unconditionally trusting a frozen record or stale ID cannot.

findings.title: Git hygiene admits broad staging through a pathspec delimiter.
findings.assessment: The policy refuses broad options before -- but accepts any nonempty path list after it, including git add -- . . Attached -Cfoo is not consumed as a global option and can bypass recognition of a protected subcommand. The policy is a token heuristic rather than a complete Git command admission grammar.
findings.limits: No Git commands executed. The direct argv witness is independent of shell parsing; broader shell wrapping remains outside this helper.

findings.title: Ownership-first reconciliation needs an explicit authoritative premise.
findings.assessment: Owned paths select the branch even when only main changed; foreign-owned paths select main even when only branch changed. Only unowned paths use ordinary three-way equality rules. Therefore fail-closed concurrent-edit language is conditional on ownership-map authority, not a general preservation property.
findings.limits: This can be intentional policy rather than a defect when exclusive ownership is authoritative and current. The control does not execute Git or claim any actual edit was lost.
findings.next_action: State and verify ownership freshness/exclusivity, bind the map into the candidate, and distinguish policy-selected discard from conflict-free content preservation.

A benign allowed token can therefore hide a separate disallowed local path on the same line. The four regex profiles also deliberately cover only selected path spellings.
